title: Actual derived open counit on a closed pushforward supported in the open
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $Y,U,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow U$ be a closed immersion such that $k=ji:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is also closed [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $B$ be a sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_Z$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Put $F=k_*B$ and $G=i_*B$, using [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $j^{-1}$ be ordinary inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $j_!$ extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. There is a canonical restriction isomorphism $\rho:j^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ whose component at every etale $V\to U$ is the identity on $B(V\times_U Z)$, after the canonical fibre-product identification. The sheaf $F$ restricts to zero on $Y\setminus k(Z)$.

On the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use the adjunction $Dj_!\dashv D(j^{-1})$ obtained by localizing the sheaf adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] (both functors are exact on module sheaves over the constant ring sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]) as in [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. Denote its counit by $\epsilon_M:Dj_!D(j^{-1})M\to M$. On sheaves this is the localized original sheaf counit. With sheaves placed in degree zero, the actual morphism
$$e=\epsilon_F\circ Dj_!(\rho^{-1}):Dj_!G\longrightarrow F$$
is an isomorphism. For every $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and every morphism $c:F\to M$, set $c_U=D(j^{-1})(c)\circ\rho^{-1}:G\to D(j^{-1})M$. Then the actual derived morphisms satisfy
$$\epsilon_M\circ Dj_!(c_U)=c\circ e.$$
This applies in particular to shifted sheaves $M=L[r]$ for every integer $r$.

proof.text: Construct the canonical isomorphism between the pullbacks of V.hom and i over U and of V.hom ≫ j and i ≫ j over Y using pullback.lift in both directions, cancellation of the monomorphism j, and pullback.hom_ext. Its two projection equations imply naturality in V. Apply the presheaf B contravariantly, lift the resulting natural isomorphism to sheaves, and compose it with upperStarIsoOpenImmersionRestriction. Cancellation of that restriction comparison proves exactly the required section formula.

proof.text: Put $W=Y\setminus k(Z)$, which is open because $k$ is closed. For every etale $T\to W$, the fibre product $T\times_Y Z$ is empty: a point of it would map both into $W$ and into $k(Z)$. Hence $F(T)=B(\varnothing)=0$, the last equality being the sheaf axiom for the empty covering of the empty object. Restriction to $W$ is the inverse image along its open inclusion, by the restriction description of the cited adjunction. It follows that $F|_W=0$.

proof.text: Check the original sheaf counit on all geometric stalks using Scheme.isIso_of_isIso_sheafFiber_map. For a point inside j(U), lift it through j; the upperStar image of the counit is already invertible by the triangle identity and the invertible open-adjunction unit. Transfer this invertibility to the stalk using upperStarCompUliftSheafFiberIso. Outside j(U), the extension-by-zero source stalk vanishes. The point also lies in the open complement W of the closed image of i ≫ j. The existing disjoint-range vanishing lemma gives W^*(i ≫ j)_* B = 0; lifting the point through W and the same fibre comparison show the target stalk is zero. The stalk map is therefore invertible in ModuleCat, so conservativity applies directly to module sheaves.

proof.text: Apply the sheaf adjunction termwise to the degree-zero single complex F. Its counit components are invertible: in degree zero transport the preceding sheaf result by singleObjXSelf, and in every other degree both objects are zero. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isIso_of_components makes the complex counit invertible. Expand exactDerivedAdjunction using Adjunction.localization_counit_app: the derived counit is a composite of the standard exact-functor comparison isomorphisms and the localization of this invertible complex counit. Finally the inverse restriction isomorphism and its standard degree-zero comparison remain invertible under the derived extension-by-zero functor. Their composite is precisely closedSupportOpenCounitArrow.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), exact-functor localization; specified counit convention in def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction.

proof.text: Write $J=Dj_!$ and $P=D(j^{-1})$. The counit of the specified derived adjunction is a natural transformation $JP\to\mathrm{id}$; its defining naturality equation at the arbitrary derived morphism $c:F\to M$ is $\epsilon_M\circ JP(c)=c\circ\epsilon_F$. Functoriality and the definition of $c_U$ give $\epsilon_M\circ J(c_U)=\epsilon_M\circ JP(c)\circ J(\rho^{-1})=c\circ\epsilon_F\circ J(\rho^{-1})=c\circ e$. Naturality here is in the derived category itself, so $c$ need not be represented by a sheaf map or an unlocalized chain map. Taking $M=L[r]$ gives the asserted shifted-sheaf case for every integer $r$.
